title: Shadow IT Detection
exclusions: Sees only traffic through the web gateway, and domains rather than individual applications. Secure Access App Discovery gives application-level risk scores; use it alongside this report.
evidence: Weekly report export and the governance decision (approve, replace, block) recorded for each domain with 10 or more users.

controlTest.positiveScenario: From three test users behind the web gateway, sign in to and upload a small file to a file-sharing service that is not in `approved_saas_domains.csv`. After the next S3 sync the search returns one row for that domain with `users` of 3 and `upload_mb` above zero.
controlTest.negativeScenario: Repeat with a domain that is in the lookup with `approved=true`. The requests are indexed, but the domain does not appear in the results.

dataSources: `index=sse sourcetype=cisco:cloud_security:proxy` (or `cisco:umbrella:proxy` on older Umbrella exports) from the Secure Access or Umbrella S3 log bucket, read by the Cisco Secure Access Add-on (7569). One event per web request through the secure web gateway with `action`, `url`, `url_domain`, `category`, `blocked_category`, `user`, `identities`, `src_ip`, `bytes_in`, `bytes_out`, `http_method`, and `status`, tagged `web` and `proxy` for the CIM Web data model.
app: Cisco Secure Access Add-on for Splunk ([Splunkbase 7569](https://splunkbase.splunk.com/app/7569)), which reads Cisco Secure Access and Cisco Umbrella logs from the S3 log bucket and maps the web proxy log to the CIM Web data model. The companion Cisco Secure Access App (Splunkbase 5558) adds dashboards.
spl:
index=sse sourcetype IN ("cisco:cloud_security:proxy", "cisco:umbrella:proxy")
| eval action=lower(action)
| where action="allowed" AND isnotnull(url_domain)
| stats dc(user) as users sum(bytes_out) as bytes_out sum(bytes_in) as bytes_in values(category) as categories by url_domain
| lookup approved_saas_domains.csv url_domain OUTPUT approved
| where isnull(approved) AND users >= 3
| eval upload_mb=round(bytes_out/1048576, 1)
| sort - users
description: Lists destination domains reached through the Secure Access or Umbrella web gateway by three or more users that are not in the approved SaaS lookup, with user count, upload volume, and categories.
value: Unapproved cloud services hold company data outside contracts, retention, and access control. Ranking unknown domains by how many people use them and how much they upload shows which ones to approve, replace, or block first.
implementation: Collect the web proxy log with the Cisco Secure Access Add-on (7569) into `index=sse` and maintain `approved_saas_domains.csv` with `url_domain` and `approved`. Run weekly as a report for the governance team.
visualization: Table: url_domain, users, upload_mb, categories. Supporting panel: count of unapproved domains with 10 or more users over 90 days (line chart).
cimSpl:
| tstats summariesonly=true dc(Web.user) as users sum(Web.bytes_out) as bytes_out values(Web.category) as categories from datamodel=Web where Web.action="allowed" by Web.url_domain
| rename Web.url_domain as url_domain
| lookup approved_saas_domains.csv url_domain OUTPUT approved
| where isnull(approved) AND users >= 3
dataModelAcceleration: Enable acceleration on the CIM Web data model over `index=sse` before using the tstats variant.

references.title: Cisco Secure Access Add-on for Splunk (Splunkbase 7569)
Cisco Umbrella: Log Management and Amazon S3 log export
Splunk: Integrated Enterprise Value for Cisco data (supported source types)

knownFalsePositives:
1. **CDNs and shared infrastructure** — content delivery and analytics domains are used by every site and appear with many users. Add them to the lookup as approved infrastructure.

2. **Sub-domains of approved services** — `url_domain` may be a regional or tenant sub-domain of an approved service. Normalise to the registered domain in the lookup.

**Suppression:** the approved lookup itself; review additions quarterly.
detailedImplementation:
Prerequisites
• Cisco Secure Access Add-on for Splunk (Splunkbase 7569) on the search heads and on the heavy forwarder or Inputs Data Manager that reads the S3 bucket.
• Log export to Amazon S3 enabled in the Secure Access or Umbrella dashboard (Admin > Log Management), either a Cisco-managed bucket or your own, with the access key and secret for Splunk.
• An index for Secure Access and Umbrella data (this page uses `index=sse`) and a role with `srchIndexesAllowed` on it for the network security team.
• A lookup `approved_saas_domains.csv` with columns `url_domain` and `approved`, owned by the governance team.

Step 1 — Configure data collection
• In the add-on create an S3 modular input for the web proxy log path with the bucket name, region, access key, and secret, and set the index to `sse`.
• Logs reach S3 in batches, so events usually arrive in Splunk 10 to 15 minutes after the request. `action` is logged as Allowed or Blocked (ALLOWED or BLOCKED in some exports); the searches lowercase it.
• Check the fields this search needs: run `index=sse sourcetype="cisco:cloud_security:proxy" | stats count by action` over 1 day and confirm both values appear.

Step 2 — Create the search and alert
```spl
index=sse sourcetype IN ("cisco:cloud_security:proxy", "cisco:umbrella:proxy")
| eval action=lower(action)
| where action="allowed" AND isnotnull(url_domain)
| stats dc(user) as users sum(bytes_out) as bytes_out sum(bytes_in) as bytes_in values(category) as categories by url_domain
| lookup approved_saas_domains.csv url_domain OUTPUT approved
| where isnull(approved) AND users >= 3
| eval upload_mb=round(bytes_out/1048576, 1)
| sort - users
```

Understanding this SPL
• The search keeps allowed requests only; blocked services are already under control.
• `stats` by `url_domain` counts distinct users and sums upload and download bytes per destination.
• The lookup removes approved services; the 3-user floor keeps one-off personal browsing out of the report.
• `upload_mb` highlights destinations where data is leaving, which matter more than read-only sites.

Accelerated variant over the CIM data model:
```spl
| tstats summariesonly=true dc(Web.user) as users sum(Web.bytes_out) as bytes_out values(Web.category) as categories from datamodel=Web where Web.action="allowed" by Web.url_domain
| rename Web.url_domain as url_domain
| lookup approved_saas_domains.csv url_domain OUTPUT approved
| where isnull(approved) AND users >= 3
```
• The tstats variant runs the same logic on `Web.url_domain`, `Web.user`, and `Web.bytes_out`, and works for any proxy mapped to CIM Web.

Step 3 — Validate
• Compare with the Secure Access dashboard (or the Umbrella dashboard) under Reporting > Activity Search, filtered to Web and the same time range: the totals there should match the totals here within the S3 delivery delay.
• For one domain on the report, search it in Activity Search and confirm the user count roughly matches.
• Run `index=sse sourcetype="cisco:cloud_security:proxy" | timechart span=1h count` over 7 days; gaps longer than an hour point to S3 input failures.

Step 4 — Operationalize
• Run weekly over 7 days and email to the governance team.
• For each domain with 10 or more users, record a decision in the lookup: approve, replace with a sanctioned service, or block in Secure Access.
• Track the trend panel to show the shadow IT backlog shrinking.

Step 5 — Troubleshooting
• No proxy events and S3 access errors (403 AccessDenied) in the add-on log: the access key cannot read the bucket or the region is wrong.
• Proxy events missing while DNS events arrive: the Secure Web Gateway is not enabled for those identities, or the S3 input path points at the DNS folder only.
• Events arrive hours late: the input polling interval is long, or the bucket path prefix is wrong and the input scans the whole bucket.
• `url_domain` is empty: older Umbrella exports only have `url`; derive the domain with `rex field=url "^https?://(?<url_domain>[^/:]+)"`.
• The tstats variant returns nothing while the raw search works: the Web data model is not accelerated over `index=sse`, or the `cim_Web_indexes` macro does not include it.
grandmaExplanation: We list online services several staff use that IT has not approved, so we can decide whether to allow them before company files end up there.
